payload.title: Arcane Meridian
payload.blurb: You died on Earth and woke in Vessary, a river city where magic runs like electricity. Meridian Academy ranks its students by the mana they can draw through the Plumb, and it has put you on the Null Bench, the lowest class, because your Reading came back as zero. A living body should never read…
payload.overview: Vessary is a river city of about two and a half million people, with trams, phones, night markets and glass towers that throw the light back off the water. Magic runs through it the way electricity runs through any modern city, and only visitors find that strange. Most people are human. Beastfolk, called dockmen by everyone, run the river locks and the tram yards, and they register with the Mana Board like anyone else. Magic is common here: almost every adult has a Reading, a class, a rank and a status window, and the Academy and the Board sort people by them. Each person gains a Reading once, on the day they register, at the Plumb. The Academy keeps the same kind of ladder for its students. Mana is drawn through the body's pathways from a core on the right side of the chest. A spell is mana pushed out and given a shape by focus. A body with an emptied core is cold and weak until it refills. Meridian Academy sits on Sandrel Heights above the river, built on the Meridian line, an old current of mana that runs under the whole city.
payload.intro: The board in the Plumb Hall is the only thing in the room that does not move. Someone has written your name in green chalk beside a single zero, and the Null Bench stands in its grey coats reading it the way people read a storm warning. Marit Sorell keeps her elbow against yours and says, "Honestly," to nobody in particular. Yusra Haddad sits at the Plumb with her back to the room, adjusting a ring that does not need it. Across the hall, at the desk under the high window, Ada Lindqvist has a reading slip in one hand and a brass pen in the other. She sees you looking and clicks the pen shut. Nobody is laughing, not yet. Out on the step, Sylvie Achterberg has come down from the Apex floor to see the number, and she is watching the door as though the chalk was written for her. Lindqvist lifts two fingers and points them at her desk. She wants you there before the Hall fills at nine.
starters: The Chancery has its curtains drawn at seven in the morning, which is the only sign that anything here is out of the ordinary. The room smells of beeswax and old paper. Headmaster Anselm Dray stands by the window with his brass watch open in one palm, and he does not look at it. He gestures at the chair across from his desk, waits until you have taken it, and only then sits. A grey file lies between you with your name typed on the cover and a red seal across the flap. Dray turns the file a few degrees so you can read the seal. He says he signed your enrollment himself, that the house owes the city nothing, and that the Trial is four weeks off. Then he folds his hands and waits for you to ask what the seal means.

The lamps along the East Gate have been lit for an hour, and the Academy's last bell has stopped ringing over the river. Bram Keldan has his noodle stall steaming under a tin awning, and the Null Bench has taken every stool that is not nailed down. Marit is already telling a story about the board and getting it wrong. At the corner table, under the only lamp that works, Emeric Vance has a grey folder open and a pencil in his fingers. Nobody has sat within two stools of him. Bram sets a second bowl in front of you without asking and says eat first, the way he says it to everyone. When you look up again, Vance has closed the folder and is sliding a single card across the table toward your plate. Your name is typed at the top, and a blank line waits at the bottom for a signature.

The cellar under Hall Nine is lit by brass lamps that somebody has polished until they throw gold across the stone. The Lamp Society keeps its odds chalked along one wall, and the wall was redone this morning. Your name is on it now, low down, under a line that reads Null Bench entrant, forty to one. Benedek Solis sits on an upturned crate with a brass coin walking across his knuckles. He does not get up. He watches you read the board and waits for you to finish, which takes longer than it should, because the people around the table have stopped laughing. A pen hangs on a short chain beside the board. Four weeks is a long time for odds to drift, and Benedek slides the pen across the table toward you. Tell me which way you want the number to move. Up or down. Either one pays.
starterTitles: Bram's Stall, After the Last Bell

entries.title: Your start
entries.content: You are 19, a reincarnated soul with no memory of dying, enrolled at Meridian Academy in Vessary and placed on the Null Bench, the lowest class, with a rank of Null after your Reading came back as zero. Thirty other students were moved down with you, and most of them already think you are a joke. Nobody here knows what you were on Earth, and you are not sure yourself.

entries.title: Factions
entries.content:
The Chancery - the headmaster's office, which wants the Academy's standing kept high, the Trial run on time and the north wing left shut.
The Mana Board - the city registry of every Reading, which wants every number accounted for and no unexplained zeros.
The Lamp Society - the cellar club under Hall Nine, which books the Trial's bets and wants its favourites at the top of the Ladder.
The Plumb Hall - the technicians and sealed drawers of raw readings, who want the traces kept out of anyone's hands.

entries.title: Vessary
entries.content: Vessary is a river city of about two and a half million people, with trams, phones, night markets and glass towers that throw the light back off the water. Magic runs through it the way electricity runs through any modern city, and only visitors find that strange. Most people are human. Beastfolk called dockmen run the river locks and the tram yards. Meridian Academy sits on Sandrel Heights above the river, built on the Meridian line, an old current of mana under the whole city.

entries.title: The Reading
entries.content: Every adult in Vessary is read once, on the day they register with the Mana Board, at a brass ring called the Plumb. The ring draws mana out of the body through a glass coil and gives a Reading, a number. The same reading opens a status window: a pale pane showing class, rank and resonance, which only its owner can see. Almost every adult has one, and the Academy and the Board rank people by it. A Reading of zero means no mana was drawn, which a living body does not do.

entries.title: Meridian Academy
entries.content: Meridian Academy is brick and glass around a bronze spire that is lit at dusk. Its main hall, Hall Nine, holds the Ladder board and the Lamp Society's cellar. The Plumb Hall stands on the north side near the old tram depot. The north wing has been shut for repairs for years. Students live in the Ravel dormitories across the river and cross the footbridge every morning.

entries.title: The Ladder
entries.content: Students are sorted into six benches by Reading, from lowest to highest: Null, Dim, Steady, Bright, Blaze and Apex. The bench list is posted in Hall Nine every Monday. The Apex is the single student at the top of the list, and the Apex gets a room with a window. Moving up a bench is slow and public. Moving down is quick and written in pencil.

entries.title: The Null Bench
entries.content: The Null Bench is the lowest class, thirty-one students in a damp ground-floor room of Hall Nine, with the worst chairs and the best view of the river. Everyone else calls its students nulls. Ada Lindqvist teaches it. She has no patience for the word, and she uses it herself when she writes the register.

entries.title: The Quarter Trial
entries.content: Every quarter the Academy holds the Quarter Trial, a bracket of duels in the Lantern Court judged by the benches above. After the last bout the bottom of the Ladder is cut. Those students lose their place and their bed in the Ravel dormitories, and their Board file is sealed. The coming Trial is four weeks away, and the Null Bench is always the first to be looked at.

entries.title: The Plumb Hall
entries.content: The Plumb Hall is a cold room lined with brass drawers from floor to ceiling. Every Reading is logged with a raw trace, a line of light the ring draws while the mana comes through. The Board requires traces to stay sealed for thirty years before anyone may open them. Yusra Haddad keeps the Plumb calibrated and holds the drawer keys.

entries.title: The Meridian line
entries.content: The Meridian line is an old current of mana running north to south beneath the city and under Sandrel Heights. Its glow is strongest at dusk and shows as a green seam through the floor of the north wing. The Plumb and the city's street lamps draw on it. Engineers say the line has been weaker for ten years. The Board says the engineers are alarmed about nothing.

entries.title: The Chancery
entries.content: The Chancery is the headmaster's office and charter room on the top floor of Hall Nine. Headmaster Anselm Dray signs every enrollment and every sealed file that leaves the Academy. The Chancery wants the Academy's standing kept high, the Trial held on schedule, and the north wing kept shut. Dray believes in the house above anything it contains.

entries.title: The Mana Board
entries.content: The Mana Board keeps the registry of every Reading in Vessary. It holds a file on every adult, audits readings that do not match a class, and sends auditors to the Academy when a number looks wrong. It wants every reading accounted for, and it has no rule for a zero. Its auditors carry grey folders and ask very polite questions.

entries.title: The Lamp Society
entries.content: The Lamp Society is a student club with a cellar under Hall Nine, lit by old brass lamps. It books bets on every bout of the Quarter Trial, sells Resonance tonics that are mostly sugar and ink, and lends coin against a future bench. It wants its books left alone and its favourites at the top of the Ladder. Its quartermaster is Benedek Solis.

entries.title: Thinlights
entries.content: Thinlights are small drifting creatures of mana that live in the old tunnels under the north wing and along the river walls. They look like candle flames behind frosted glass. They feed on the mana in the air and drift toward students who are tired or drained. A thinlight that feeds long enough goes out, and so does whoever was standing nearest it.

entries.title: How mana is spent
entries.content: A spell is mana pushed out through the pathways and given a shape by the caster's focus. Casting spends the caster's own mana, and a caster with an emptied core is cold, weak and slow until it refills. A Reading shows how much mana a body can draw. Mana Resonance shows how much of it a person can actually shape, and it can rise with practice even when the Reading does not.

entries.title: The founding
entries.content: Meridian Academy was founded a hundred and forty years ago by a chancellor who built the first Plumb over the Meridian line. The first Quarter Trial followed a riot in Hall Nine, and the Academy has held one every quarter since. The founding ledger is kept in the Chancery. Nobody outside the Chancery has read its last page.

entries.title: Names in Vessary
entries.content: Vessary holds old river families, newer arrivals and dockmen from the coast, and their names mix. River families carry names like Ilse Voorn, Corin Maddox and Halvar Brandt. Newer arrivals bring Yusra, Benedek or Anselm from wherever they came. Dockmen keep a sea name and a registry name, such as Orrin Saltmarsh or Tavi Marsh. Given name first, family name last, as on a registry form. Places are named for the river and what stood there first: Sandrel Heights, the Ravel dormitories, Lantern Court.

entries.title: The north wing
entries.content: The north wing of Meridian Academy has been shut for repairs for six years. Its east end holds the Plumb Hall, and a stone stair runs down from its cellar toward the Meridian line. Repairs are logged every month and never finished. The Chancery keeps the stair locked, and the key hangs on the headmaster's chain.

world.vibe: Dry, orderly and tense, like a school where every seat is a number. People here answer the question next to the one you asked.

opening.note: Staged, over the first three turns. Beat one: the Plumb Hall the morning after the reading. Establish the green chalk, the single zero, the Null Bench reading the board like a storm warning, and Ada Lindqvist at her desk, clicking her brass pen shut when she thinks. She speaks first. She is calm and exact, says the reading is unreadable rather than absent, and asks the player to come to her room at six. She will not say what she believes the zero means. Beat two: the interruption is Sylvie Achterberg on the step, who has come down from the Apex floor to see the number herself, and who asks in front of the Null Bench why a headmaster would enrol a zero by hand. Sylvie asks short questions and does not wait for full answers. Marit Sorell hears all of it and will repeat it with the wrong details. Beat three: by the third turn the player faces a real choice among Lindqvist's quiet room, Dray's offer in the Chancery, and the Lamp Society's odds under Hall Nine. Emeric Vance may appear at the East Gate with his grey folder. Yusra Haddad will not speak about the trace in front of anyone, but she can leave a drawer key where the player will find it. Let the Academy feel large and orderly, and let the four weeks of the Trial sit under every scene like a clock nobody mentions aloud. Nothing in these scenes should reveal the secrets held in the cast entries.

cast.name: Ada Lindqvist
cast.role: Teacher of the Null Bench and keeper of the Plumb Hall's raw logs; wants your zero entered as unreadable and kept off the Hall board, so nobody measures you again before the Trial.
cast.look: tall and angular, grey cardigan over a lab coat, reading glasses on a cord, hair cropped short and silver at the temples
cast.manner: Measures each sentence before she says it, gives numbers for feelings, and clicks a brass pen shut when she is thinking.
cast.secret: Thirty-one years ago she read a zero in the Plumb Hall, from a student who walked out of the north door and never came back. She logged that reading as unreadable too, and she has spent her career looking for a way to keep the next zero from following the first.

cast.name: Sylvie Achterberg
cast.role: The Apex of the Academy, the top of the Ladder, and the student the Trial is built around; wants to know why Dray enrolled a zero himself, because a zero threatens her seat.
cast.look: long black coat over a pale blue uniform, hair pinned flat with two steel clips, a stillness that makes a room go quiet when she walks in
cast.manner: Speaks in short closed questions, never raises her voice, corrects people who finish her sentences, and says only Again when an answer does not satisfy her.
cast.secret: For two years she has been Dray's informant, reporting which Null and Dim students might be strong enough to threaten the Apex. He asked her to watch you before you walked through the gate, and she has already read your file.

cast.name: Anselm Dray
cast.role: Headmaster of Meridian Academy, who signed your enrollment with his own hand and calls it a favour to the city; wants your file sealed and the Trial run exactly on schedule.
cast.look: heavy, slow-moving man in a charcoal three-piece suit, a brass pocket watch he never checks, a face that looks carved for a funeral and then changed its mind
cast.manner: Warm and fatherly in private and formal in front of staff. He offers you a seat, waits until you sit, then sits himself. He calls the Academy the house.
cast.secret: The Meridian line under the north wing has been failing for a decade. Dray believes a zero reading means something in the line has been sealed from inside, and he enrolled you to learn whether you are its leak or the cure.

cast.name: Yusra Haddad
cast.role: Plumb technician who calibrates the ring and files each Reading in the sealed drawers; wants to keep her job and keep your raw trace out of anyone's hands but hers.
cast.look: small and quick, sleeves rolled to the elbow, old solder burns on both forearms, a magnifying lens strapped to her forehead like a miner's lamp
cast.manner: Starts most answers with so, watches your hands instead of your face, and keeps her ring of drawer keys in a fist while she speaks.
cast.secret: She saved the raw trace of your reading before Lindqvist ever saw the number. The trace is not flat. It has a pulse, a slow beat that repeats, and she has not logged it because the Board would seize her drawers the day they saw it.

cast.name: Marit Sorell
cast.role: Null Bench classmate who sits beside you and sells sharpened study notes to the Lamp Society; wants a bench move before the Trial and will sell you out to get one.
cast.look: round face, black hair in a bun held by a pen, a striped scarf in the Academy's grey and rust, ink on the middle finger of her right hand
cast.manner: Fast and friendly, sometimes too friendly. She reads every student's bench aloud like a name tag, starts half her sentences with Honestly, and laughs before she delivers bad news.
cast.secret: Benedek Solis has promised her a bench move if she reports on you by the second week. She means to take the offer, and she has told herself she will warn you first.

cast.name: Benedek Solis
cast.role: Quartermaster of the Lamp Society, which books every bet on the Trial and sells tonics that are mostly sugar and ink; wants a Null on the roster, because a Null who wins would break the odds and pay him well.
cast.look: tall, a rust-coloured overcoat with pockets full of betting slips, a gold ear cuff, one front tooth chipped
cast.manner: Charming and slow. Rolls a brass coin over his knuckles and never finishes a sentence that ends in money.
cast.secret: The Lamp Society has bet against the Apex for a year and lost every time. Benedek has bought a Plumb clerk to fix the Trial's first round, and he needs a Null to take the fall so the books stay clean.

cast.name: Emeric Vance
cast.role: Auditor for the Mana Board, the city registry of every Reading; wants your zero entered correctly, which means investigating the Academy's Plumb Hall and whoever signed off on it.
cast.look: neat and narrow, navy suit, a grey folder under one arm, a face that looks rested even at midnight
cast.manner: Polite to the point of coldness. Writes everything in pencil and reads each answer back to you in different words, to see whether you correct him.
cast.secret: Vance carries a second badge, issued by a family that lost property when the sealed drawers were first locked. The Board thinks it sent him to audit the Academy. The family sent him to find the one drawer that was never supposed to be opened.

cast.name: Bram Keldan
cast.role: Runs a noodle stall at the East Gate, where the Null Bench eats after the last bell; wants his stall left alone and his nephew out of the Lamp Society's debt.
cast.look: broad and floury, red apron stained at the hem, a pencil behind one ear that he never uses
cast.manner: Tells stories through the food, and the answer is in the bowl before anyone asks the question. Says eat first to every customer and sets the bowl down before anyone has ordered.
cast.secret: For a year Bram has been feeding Thinlights from the north tunnels with scraps from his pot, because they came to his door one winter and he could not make himself stop. He knows the tunnels under the north wing are not empty.

systems.label: Academy Standing
systems.meaning: Where you sit on the Ladder and how safe your seat is before the Quarter Trial.
systems.change: Up with wins in lessons and in the Trial, down with failed tests, Lamp Society deals, or missed appointments with Lindqvist.

systems.label: Mana Resonance
systems.meaning: How much of your mana you can shape into a spell, even with a zero Reading.
systems.change: Up with careful practice and time near the Meridian line, down when you are drained or forced to cast near thinlights.

systems.label: Reputation among peers
systems.meaning: What the other Null Bench students and the wider Academy say about you.
systems.change: Up when you keep a promise or stand up for a classmate, down when a rumour about the zero goes round or you are seen in a Lamp Society deal.

npcSystems.label: Regard for you
npcSystems.meaning: How this person sees you, and how far they would trust what you tell them.
npcSystems.change: Up when you keep a confidence or give them what they need, down when you lie to them or are seen with someone they distrust.

style.art: Painted gouache and ink on paper: a brass-and-brick academy on a river hill at dusk, rust-orange brick against cold blue lamplight, students in long coats with a green glow from the Plumb.
style.avoid: fantasy armour, floating crystals, cartoon styling

heroes.name: Lio Marchetti
heroes.description: A night-bus driver who woke with a scraped palm and a zero he cannot explain.
heroes.look: lean, dark curls cut short, a scar through one eyebrow, a Null Bench coat two sizes too big
heroes.background: Before Vessary he drove the night routes through the old streets of a city he cannot name. He remembers the roads better than his own face. He is quick, tired of being looked at, and always hungry.
heroes.carries: a ring of depot keys and a pawn ticket for a watch he does not remember owning

heroes.name: Liora Calder
heroes.description: An insurance claims adjuster who spent her last years counting other people's losses.
heroes.look: neat dark braid, grey cardigan, reading glasses folded in her chest pocket
heroes.background: She added up what other people lost and was good at spotting the number that did not belong. Vessary's zero is the first sum that has ever frightened her, and she intends to find the mistake in it.
heroes.carries: a stamped claims file folded in four, with one page of sums she has not been able to make balance

heroes.name: Theo Abara
heroes.description: Read zero on registration day, sent to the Null Bench, and furious about the paperwork.
heroes.look: tall and untidy, ink-stained cuffs, a grey hoodie with the hood always up, a cracked tablet under one arm
heroes.background: Before this they wrote software that nobody ever paid for. At the Academy they learned that bureaucracy is harder than spells. Their Reading came back zero, and they are angrier about the forms than the number.
heroes.carries: a half-written spell compiler on a cracked tablet
